newsitem.title: USA: Thermo Electron unit's ProTime gets FDA okay.
newsitem.headline: Thermo Electron unit's ProTime gets FDA okay.

text.p: International Technidyne Corp said its ProTime system, which measures the clotting activity of blood, received marketing clearance from the Food and Drug Administration to be sold for home use.
It said the device could be used by up to two million patients on oral anticoagulant therapy to monitor the efficacy of their treatment at home.
ProTime, a hand-held instrument, was previously approved for professional use in 1995 and has been sold to physician offices, clinics and home-care providers, the company said.

The company said that testing with ProTime at home will allow more frequent monitoring, which may result in better management of anti-blood clotting medication and may lower incidence of life-threatening complications.

The FDA's approval, it said, gives physicians the option for either in-office or at-home monitoring. Regular monitoring by the patient at home will also guide physicians with information necessary to adjust dosing and utimately reducing certain risks in medication such as gastrointestinal bleeding or strokes.
International Technidyne is a subsidiary of Thermo Biomedical, which is a unit of Thermo Electron Corp, a fast-growing player in the medical device industry.
